title: Feedback that changes what people do

sections.title: Soon, two-way, and for what went well

narration: Say a colleague's meeting ran long again.
You keep it light: "Maybe tighten it up?"
They nod. You both feel fine.
beats.visual_intent: Two peer colleagues by the meeting room door after an overrun; the giver's speech bubble with the vague line, the colleague smiles and nods, both relaxed.

grounding.claim: an illustrative overrunning meeting and a vague friendly comment

narration: Next week, it runs over again.
Feelings changed. Behaviour didn't.
beats.visual_intent: The same meeting a week later: the wall clock passes the end time again, the same colleague still talking; the nod from b01 is not enough.

grounding.claim: a pleasant talk is not evidence that anything changed

beats.delivery: a beat of wry understatement on the second line
beats.misconception: a friendly talk ending in a nod means the feedback worked

narration: Here's how to make your next talk stick.
beats.visual_intent: The presenter, warm and direct, makes the promise in one line.

grounding.claim: the promise: feedback can be shaped to change what happens next

narration: A nod isn't evidence.
General feedback tends not to change behaviour:
it doesn't say what to repeat.
on_screen: A nod is not a change
beats.visual_intent: The nod from b01 freezes; a general comment bubble floats with nothing in it to act on, no action highlighted.

grounding.claim: general feedback tends not to change behaviour because it names no specific action
a nod is not evidence of change

beats.misconception: a friendly talk ending in a nod means the feedback worked

narration: "You're disorganised" is about the person.
That kind tends to work worst.
"We ran twenty minutes over" is what you saw.
on_screen: What you saw: "Ran twenty minutes over"
beats.visual_intent: Side by side about the same meeting: a label stuck on the colleague (they bristle) versus the clock showing the overrun (they look at it). The seen side is marked as the one to use.

grounding.claim: feedback aimed at the person is most linked to weak or negative effects
useful feedback describes what was seen or heard, not character
twenty minutes over is an illustration

concepts: about the person versus about the action

narration: Think of your last "good job".
Could they say what to repeat?
beats.visual_intent: A quiet frame: a thumbs-up note on a desk, with an empty space where the specific action would be. The viewer thinks.

recall.prompt: Think of the last 'good job' you gave. Could they say what to do again?

grounding.claim: general praise does not say which action to repeat

narration: Now rebuild it, part by part.
The situation and what you saw:
"Tuesday's meeting ran twenty minutes over."
on_screen: Tuesday's meeting ran twenty minutes over.
beats.visual_intent: The vague bubble from b01 becomes a message card; its first line appears as spoken (situation and behaviour), and the colleague's face shifts from easy to attentive.

grounding.claim: name the situation and the observed behaviour
describe what could be seen

narration: Then the impact, on the work or people:
"Two people missed their next call."
on_screen: Two people missed their next call.
beats.visual_intent: The same message card grows a second line, the accent; behind it two people hurry out late to a call. The colleague's expression turns thoughtful: now it matters.

grounding.claim: impact is what the behaviour did to the work, people or results

narration: Situation, behaviour, impact: one known structure, SBI.
It stops at impact, so add a step.
beats.visual_intent: The two lines on the card are labelled with their parts, the SBI name shown once and small; an empty third slot opens below.

grounding.claim: SBI structures feedback as situation, behaviour and impact; one established structure
SBI stops at impact; the next step is an addition

narration: A concrete next step, agreed together:
"Could we try a timed agenda?"
Specific goals beat "do your best".
on_screen: Could we try a timed agenda?
beats.visual_intent: The third line fills the slot on the same card; the colleague nods again, but this time picks up a pen and writes the agenda times. Complete message: three lines.

grounding.claim: effective feedback points forward with what to do next
specific goals lead to better performance than 'do your best'

narration: Say a handover note left out a client deadline.
Which line would change what happens next?
on_screen: Which line changes what happens next?
B: The handover could have been better.
C: Your note skipped the deadline; it slipped. List it next time?
beats.visual_intent: A different moment: a handover note with a missing deadline line. Three option cards, A, B, C, held still through the pause.

recall.question: Which line would change what happens next?
options: B: The handover could have been better.
C: Your note skipped the deadline; it slipped. List it next time?

grounding.claim: an illustrative handover moment for transfer

beats.delivery: brisk on the setup, then silence

narration: C has the behaviour, impact and a next step.
B is polite, with nothing to act on.
A is about the person; it invites defence.
on_screen: B: polite, nothing to act on
beats.visual_intent: C is marked right and its three parts light up; B fades with an empty outline where the parts should be; A is marked wrong, the recipient folds their arms.

grounding.claim: behaviour, impact and next step make feedback actionable
general feedback names no action
person-focused feedback is linked to weak effects and invites defence
character labels invite defence

narration: Say it soon, in private.
Then ask how they saw it, and listen,
so the next step is agreed.
beats.visual_intent: Back with the two colleagues the same afternoon, a quiet corner: the giver asks, the colleague talks, the giver listens; the next-step line on the card is edited together.

grounding.claim: give feedback soon, in a private and calm moment
two-way: ask how they saw it and listen so the next step is agreed

narration: Praise isn't just being nice.
"Great job" names nothing to repeat;
specific praise says what to keep.
beats.visual_intent: A plain 'Great job' bubble beside a specific one that points at the exact thing done well; only the specific one connects to the action.
beats.misconception: feedback is for fixing problems; praise is just being nice

grounding.claim: specific positive feedback tells the person what worked so they can keep doing it

narration: Behaviour, impact, next step, then ask.
Pick one talk you owe this week
and draft it that way first.
beats.visual_intent: The completed message card shrinks to a blank card for the viewer, its four slots ready to fill.

recall.prompt: Behaviour, impact, next step: and then ask how they saw it.

grounding.claim: the structure built in the lesson
the next step and the two-way check

narration: Next week, the meeting ends on time.
"The timed agenda got us out on time."
Behaviour changed. Relationship intact.
beats.visual_intent: The same meeting room a week on: the clock shows the end time, people leave on time; the giver tells the colleague the specific praise, both smile, easy as before.

grounding.claim: specific positive feedback names what to keep doing
the changed meeting is an illustration
